sections.content:
Population change in Bath and North East Somerset in 2032

The population in Bath and North East Somerset is projected to increase from 195,988 people in 2022 to 212,527 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 15,393 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Bath and North East Somerset
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Bath and North East Somerset, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 320, with 17,728 births and 18,048 deaths in Bath and North East Somerset between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Bath and North East Somerset by 0.2%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 2,135, with 197,111 people moving to the area and 194,976 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Bath and North East Somerset by 1.1%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is not projected to change the population substantially, with 12,915 people moving to the area and 13,037 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 15,393, with 33,773 people moving to the area and 18,380 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Bath and North East Somerset by 7.9%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Bath and North East Somerset in 2032

The median age in Bath and North East Somerset is projected to rise from 39 years in 2022 to 40 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 20% of the population in Bath and North East Somerset are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 18% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Bath and North East Somerset between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Bath and North East Somerset is projected to stay the same, at around 65%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 282 to 291 over the same time period.

This is around average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Bath and North East Somerset?

In 2032, 18% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 20% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Bath and North East Somerset between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 5% to 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 7% to 6%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 6%
